title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, board chair
originalTitle: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, board chair
content:
In its statement, the Nvidia board reiterated that it has retained independent counsel and form a committee of independent directors to investigate what it calls Huang’s targeting by “a foreign intelligence effort.” The company has also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee to “oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” and is seeking to hire a new Chief Compliance Officer position.

Huang’s tenure at Nvidia dates back to the company’s founding in 1993, when he and three co-founders were focused on the then-nascent field of GPU hardware aimed at PC gamers. In the decades since, the highly parallel cores in those GPUs have been embraced first by cryptocurrency miners and then AI companies, propelling the company to the most valuable in the world at its October peak.

Huang’s return in some ways echoes that of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who was fired almost exactly three years ago after the board said it had “no longer has confidence in his ability to continue leading OpenAI.” Two weeks later, Altman was back at the helm after many employees threatened a mass revolt and departure if he wasn’t brought back.

In Huang’s case, the revolt following his departure came not from employees but from fellow titans of the AI industry. Executives including Altman, OpenAI president Greg Brockman, xAI’s Elon Musk and Anduril’s Palmer Luckey are among the prominent industry figures that have publicly offered him support in the days since his resignation.

Nvidia stock, which had sunk roughly 25 percent since Huang’s resignation was announced, was up nearly 40 percent in pre-market trading in the immediate aftermath of Huang’s reinstatement announcement.

This is a breaking story and will be updated with additional information
